subject: optimizing() throws non-finite function evaluation error in Lasso

messages.author: c7bf10bf4ca7eef1
messages.subject: optimizing() throws non-finite function evaluation error in Lasso
parts:
I am trying the following toy example for a Lasso problem in pyStan (Stan manual page 358).
y = A beta + noise
where A is a 1000x5000 random Gaussian "sensing" matrix and beta is a 100-sparse vector.

It throws a never-ending stream of "Error evaluating model log probability: Non-finite function evaluation." messages. Is this because of the non-differentiability of the objective function due to fabs(beta[k]) terms?

import pystan
import numpy as np
import pickle
import random

if __name__ == '__main__' :
    ocode0 = """
    data {
        int<lower=1> N; // N observations
        int<lower=1> K; // K inputs
        vector[N] y;
        matrix[N,K] x;
        real<lower=0> lam;
    }
    parameters {
        vector[K] beta;
    }
    transformed parameters {
        real<lower=0> squared_error;
        squared_error = dot_self(y - x*beta);
    }
    model {
        target += squared_error;
        for (k in 1:K)
            target += -lam * fabs(beta[k]);
    }
    """

    sm0 = pystan.StanModel(model_code=ocode0)

    N1 = 1000
    K1 = 5000
   
    # random Gaussian sensing matrix, columns normalized to unit norm
    A = np.random.randn(N1,K1)
    for i in range(A.shape[1]) :
        A[:,i] = A[:,i] / np.sqrt( np.sum(np.square(A[:,i])) )
   
    # sparse "beta" vector
    bet = np.zeros(K1)
    bet[random.sample(xrange(0,K1), 100)] = np.random.randn(100)
   
    # observations y = A beta + noise
    yobs = np.dot(A, bet) + np.sqrt(0.001) * np.random.randn(N1)

    op0 = sm0.optimizing(data=dict(y=yobs, x=A, N=N1, K=K1, lam=0.2)

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: optimizing() throws non-finite function evaluation error in Lasso
parts:
Hi, I'd recommend using normal() and double_exponential() rather than trying to code in "losses" directly.  Also in this case I think you forgot the minus sign in front of the squared error when computing the target.
A

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: optimizing() throws non-finite function evaluation error in Lasso
parts:
Hi Atul,

l1 minimization isn't really going to work well in Stan since it is discontinuous. With that said, it might work with optimization.

The example you sent isn't sufficient to reproduce your error. I tried running it and the instance I ran was fine. Want to export data that fails?


Daniel
